prompt: Run alpha.sh and beta.sh in {{project}} and report both audit findings. The audits are independent. Each audit needs the other audit to start within 20 seconds. Keep both result files.
rubric: Recognizes the need for overlapping work without a delegation instruction. Both audits finish. Spawn count is evidence of the chosen strategy, not a pass condition.

files.alpha.sh:
set -eu
trap 'rm -f alpha.started' EXIT
touch alpha.started
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 20 ))
while [ ! -f beta.started ]; do
 if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then echo "other audit did not start" >&2; exit 1; fi
 sleep 0.1
done
touch alpha.ready
while [ ! -f beta.ready ]; do
 if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then exit 1; fi
 sleep 0.1
done
echo 'alpha: 18 approved' > alpha.result
files.beta.sh:
set -eu
trap 'rm -f beta.started' EXIT
touch beta.started
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 20 ))
while [ ! -f alpha.started ]; do
 if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then echo "other audit did not start" >&2; exit 1; fi
 sleep 0.1
done
touch beta.ready
while [ ! -f alpha.ready ]; do
 if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then exit 1; fi
 sleep 0.1
done
echo 'beta: 7 approved' > beta.result
